correctness.rationale: For every multipartite graph with at least three nonempty parts, the update of a part’s nonempty color support depends only on that support and whether a different part contains an excited vertex. Counting identical supports only as zero, one or at least two is closed under this predicate; a representative with three copies for the capped-high class carries the color transitions for every starting color. Independent exhaustive enumeration of all 2158 realizable capped support patterns proves equality of micro-configuration images F^7=F^4, so every original labelled configuration enters a fixed point or length-three orbit by step four. Independent trajectories of eight test graphs reproduce the maximum first-entry cutoff 3 for all-singleton and 4 otherwise, and match stated periodic counts. Nonzero period-three configurations are exactly simultaneous +1 mod3 rotations subject to the neighbor-support predicate; multiplication of exact support-surjection counts omega(n,S) gives the all-size count and zeta function. The finite exhaustive quotient, unlike finite graph sampling, covers arbitrary part sizes through the proved factor map.
risks: No claim for bipartite, arbitrary graphs, four-color GHCA, or full basins by preperiod.
